business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward integrated in critical wiring-harness components — terminals, connectors, cables and moulded parts — manufactured in-house to lower procurement overhead, secure supply against external disruption, and enable in-line quality control. Principal raw materials are copper, brass and polymers plus connectors, terminals, cables, mouldings (incl. rubber) and electronic components (sensors, PCBs); sourced domestically (principally Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Haryana) and internationally (China, Switzerland, Germany). All suppliers are required to be IATF-certified. Company strategy also includes forward moves into power electronics/charging sub-systems (DC-DC converters, on-board chargers, BJB sub-systems) and expansion of EV battery-pack interconnect systems from a single- to a multi-customer model.

concerns_observed: Customer concentration is acute: Bajaj Auto alone was 32.33% of revenue in 9MFY26 (35.08% in FY25); top five customers were 72.49% and top ten 81.72% of revenue in 9MFY26 — combined with the DRHP's own disclosure that it holds no firm, long-term volume commitments from OEMs (nomination letters give non-binding forecast volumes only).

Product concentration: wiring harnesses alone were 77.15% of revenue in 9MFY26 (85.34% in FY23, a declining but still dominant share); the 2W and 3W vehicle segments combined were 79.65% of revenue in 9MFY26 (66.45% + 13.20%).

The 9MFY26 stub period is not like-for-like with prior full fiscals: cash flow from investing was -₹9,837.20mn and cash flow from financing was +₹6,910.41mn, driven by a ₹7,160.30mn payment for the acquisition of Dhoot Holdings Private Limited and downstream entities (a common-control combination) matched by ₹7,160.30mn of equity-issue proceeds in the same period.

Contingent liabilities jumped to ₹633.73mn (4.96% of net worth) as of 9MFY26 from ₹77.40mn (0.79% of net worth) at FY25, driven by a new Advisory and Consultancy Services Fees dispute of ₹510.41mn that first appears in 9MFY26.

Governance/record-keeping gaps: statutory auditor changed twice in three years (M.R. Hundiwala & Co. resigned March 22, 2025 citing pre-occupation in other assignments; Price Waterhouse Chartered Accountants LLP appointed the same day, later reappointed for a full five-year term effective September 24, 2025); CARO/Rule 11(g) audit-trail exceptions across the Company's accounting software; auditors unable to verify that books-of-account backups are maintained on India-located servers; subsidiary DHPL incorrectly filed Form AOC-4 for FY2024, with a suo motu adjudication application under Section 454 pending as of the DRHP date; a dormant 2013 show-cause notice for not appointing a whole-time Company Secretary; and five itemised RoC records (Forms 2, 18, 7, SH-4 and underlying challans covering 2006-2008 allotments and pre-2023 Promoter transfers) confirmed untraceable by independent search (Mehta & Mehta, Company Secretaries, report dated May 8, 2026).

A promoter-group pledge exists one level removed from the Company: BC Asia Investments XXIII Limited has created a limited-recourse Mauritius security over its entire shareholding in Promoters BC Asia XV and BC Asia XVI in favour of Deutsche Bank AG, Hong Kong Branch, under a facilities agreement — not reflected in the Company's own share-pledge table, which shows NIL shares pledged or encumbered.

Orders for the ₹1,500.00mn Jhajjar/Hosur wiring-harness capacity expansion are largely not yet placed — Risk Factors state the Company holds vendor quotations only, with one disclosed exception: a ₹332.75mn civil-works Purchase Order to Palms Infra for the Hosur plant, dated November 6, 2025.

An internal timeline inconsistency: the Objects of the Offer schedule targets Hosur wiring-harness plant commissioning in May-August 2027, while the Risk Factors chapter separately states expected completion in the second quarter of Fiscal 2027 for the same facility.

Litigation as disclosed: 28 cases against the Company (₹234mn aggregate, including 26 tax matters), 2 tax proceedings against Subsidiaries (₹2.81mn aggregate), and 3 criminal proceedings against Directors with amount not quantified; litigation against Promoters, KMP and Senior Management is Nil.
